notes: Exact identifier rules mapped declarations, re-export barrels, imports, JSX uses, and test callers.
Type-alias syntax was additionally probed with the contextual pattern `type PolarityTokenPath = $T` because a kind:identifier rule does not match TypeScript type_identifier nodes.

The TS and TSX scans contained planted known-positive controls such as THEME_DERIVATION and RevealGate, so zero-call-site results for the three orphan candidates were measured rather than an empty scan.

notes: A second unrestricted literal search including non-TS files found PolarityTokenPath only in the generated index and its generator string.
Text counts include declarations, prop/type names, comments, and unrelated homonyms for generic names such as Table and Pause; they corroborate presence and absence but do not decide liveness.

summary.conclusion: No deletion is justified. The three orphan exports are intentional package API surfaces with explicit anatomy or generated-map provenance. The 43 test-only exports divide into 37 public component/framework entrypoints and six proof-facing exports, one of which also has live runtime consumers. The rot lens is accurate as a candidate generator; treating candidate status as deletion authority would produce 46 false-positive deletions.

false_positives.explanation: No candidate is falsely labeled under the lens's narrow meanings of orphan-export or test-only-export. Every label matches the semantic graph inspected. All 46 are non-actionable for deletion because package entrypoints and proof seams are deliberately retained contracts.

false_negatives.explanation: No missed caller was found for these candidates by the independent ast-grep TS+TSX pass or the 7,865-file word-bounded text scan. This is bounded to the reported candidate set and does not claim completeness outside the tool's 368-file authored-root UI scope.
